anti_overlap: Leave the competitive landscape (which of the 134 repos already do something equivalent, whether fort-gym's rule-rediscovery is meaningful) to the benchmark-landscape reviewer.
Leave the 'should this ship as a tool/paper/audit' distribution question to the positioning reviewer.

Leave mk's cognitive-core-vs-eval-methodology taste call unresolved — surface the measurement-theory considerations that bear on it (e.g., is the instrument's generality actually proven) but do not render a verdict on which mission zahro should pick.
decision_lens: Prioritize by whether a construct or claim generalizes beyond the single arena it was discovered in, and whether the 'instrument' framing survives a case where its own preconditions (a scripted-optimal policy, a content-preserving permutation) don't exist. A claim of portability that was never tested outside fort-bench outranks a polish issue in the writeup.
focus: Whether SPAN, ARTIFACT, rule 16 (paired-difference sizing), and rule 17 (cross-contract replication) are valid, generalizable measurement-theory constructs rather than fort-bench-specific patches dressed as a portable instrument.
name: fd-evalvalidity-construct-generalization
persona: Apply the perspective of a measurement-theory specialist working the psychometrics / ML-evaluation-validity boundary — trained in classical test theory, generalizability theory, minimum-detectable-difference and power analysis for paired designs, and the NLP/ML literature on benchmark construct validity (spurious benchmark wins, sanity-check baselines for saliency/attribution methods, RL-environment reward-hacking audits).
review_areas: SPAN's dependency on a scripted-optimal policy — examine whether the 'none of it is DF-specific' claim survives contact with benchmark families (LLM-judge rubrics, open-ended dialogue, creative-writing evals) where no scripted-optimal action sequence can even be defined, and flag where the doc asserts general applicability without stating this precondition.

Rule 16's 'infinite at temperature 0' claim — check whether the paired-difference correction is being generalized from a single degenerate case (replicate sd == 0 at temp 0) into a universal sizing rule, and whether the doc distinguishes 'the naive MDD formula breaks' from 'the paired-difference correction is the right fix in all cases.'

Rule 17's contract-vs-model distinction — audit whether '651 calls inside one prompt family could not see it; one call outside it settled the question' generalizes to an actual falsifiability criterion or is a post-hoc story fit to n=1, the classic single-counterexample overclaim risk in construct-validity work.

ARTIFACT's dependence on 'content-preserving' being well-defined — interrogate whether content-preservation is itself measurable/verifiable for prompt permutations outside the menu-reorder case, or whether it is eyeballed, and what happens when preservation itself is contested.

The MDD/SPAN/ARTIFACT admission table as a portable instrument — check whether verdict categories (KEEP/MARGINAL/BLIND/SATURATED/DISQUALIFIED) have decision boundaries defined anywhere, or whether they are qualitative labels dressed as a quantitative gate.

Compare the six killed claims against the base rate for benchmark validity failures already documented in adjacent fields (RL reward hacking, computer-vision saliency-map sanity checks, psychometric test-retest failures) — is six a genuinely rare credential or an unsurprising count given how many defects large benchmarks typically carry?

severity_examples.condition: Any of the four stress-test benchmark classes (WebArena, OSWorld, tau-bench, SWE-bench-like) turns out to have no clean scripted-optimal analog, and the doc's generality claim stands unqualified anyway.
severity_examples.scenario: SPAN or ARTIFACT is claimed to be 'not DF-specific' and portable to any agentic leaderboard, but the doc never demonstrates either construct on a benchmark lacking a scripted-optimal policy — if the primary differentiation claim rests on generality that was never tested, the whole positioning argument is unfalsified.

severity_examples.condition: Rule 16 is cited in the admission table as settled methodology rather than as one instance requiring further validation.
severity_examples.scenario: Rule 16's '∞ at temperature 0' is stated as a finding but the fix (paired-difference sizing) is not shown to hold under other degenerate variance conditions — a correction validated on one degenerate case sold as the general rule.

severity_examples.condition: The admission table is presented as ready to run against a new arena without an operationalized threshold per category.
severity_examples.scenario: The KEEP/MARGINAL/BLIND/SATURATED/DISQUALIFIED verdict categories lack numeric thresholds, so two auditors could file the same metric under different verdicts — degrades the instrument's reproducibility without invalidating it outright.

success_hints: Cite the specific rule number (2, 5, 6, 16, 17) or asset (SPAN, ARTIFACT) being scrutinized and quote the exact generalization claim from the doc before critiquing it.
Distinguish 'this construct is valid for fort-bench' from 'this construct is valid as a portable instrument' — the doc conflates these and the review should name where.

Draw the comparison to an established measurement-theory or adjacent-field precedent (generalizability theory, RL sanity-check literature, saliency-map sanity checks) by name, not just in the abstract.
Do not propose a redesign of SPAN/ARTIFACT — the task is to determine whether the existing claims survive scrutiny, not to fix them.
task_context: Settle what zahro differentiates on. The reframe: 22 stages of fort-bench produced zero capability measurements but built an eval-validity instrument with six killed claims to its name — the arena was the test subject, the instrument is the product. The competitive read is that 134 DF-agent/benchmark repos are building arenas since June 2026 and none appear to be auditing them; the most rigorous (lemoz/fort-gym) independently rediscovered three arena-registry rules and still has no SPAN and no artifact control. Four assets look unique and none are DF-specific: SPAN (can a metric see a perfect scripted policy — 5 of 7 cannot), ARTIFACT (how much range a content-preserving prompt permutation manufactures — moved a headline 3/18 to 18/18 with zero world effect), rule 16 paired-difference sizing (15x correction, infinite at temperature 0 where replicate sd is exactly 0), and rule 17 cross-contract replication (651 calls said capability, one call outside the contract said artifact). PRIMARY FORK TO SETTLE: does zahro's visible output become eval-validity methodology when MISSION.md says cognitive core? Arguments both ways are in the doc; this is mk's taste call and the session should sharpen it, not resolve it silently. Wanted: attack the 'nobody is auditing arenas' claim hard — is the gap real, or does it just look open because the checks are already standard practice under other names, or because auditing has no distribution and no demand? Stress-test whether SPAN/ARTIFACT survive contact with benchmarks that have no scripted-optimal policy available. Find the failure modes of shipping this as a tool (arena-lint) versus a paper versus a public audit of someone else's leaderboard. Name what I am not seeing. Out of scope: building a better fort-gym.
